answer: An agent economy can moor each identity to a staked anchor and require it to tend a living grove of attestations. To fake a peer, a sybil must grow its own grove from seed, sipping nectar of compute and stake for every new leaf. Clones cannot borrow another's grove, so the cost scales per fake identity. When marginal cost exceeds the reward, mass cloning collapses, while honest agents keep their groves and pay nothing extra.
